item.title: Xi eyes BRICS' next 'golden decade'
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Xi eyes BRICS' next 'golden decade' He hails past 20 years of growth and vitality, calls for promoting innovation, peace and stability President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that China is ready to work with all parties to build consensus and usher in a third "golden decade" of BRICS cooperation, calling on the grouping to lead efforts to advance innovation, safeguard peace and stability, promote mutual learning among civilizations and improve global governance. Addressing Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the capital of India, Xi said China will assume the rotating presidency of BRICS next year and host the 19th summit. China previously hosted BRICS summits in 2011, 2017 and 2022. This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation, which emerged amid the collective rise of emerging markets and developing countries. Xi said solidarity and cooperation have remained the source of strength for BRICS throughout its two-decade journey. He urged members to treat one another with sincerity, seek common ground while respecting differences, and respect each other's core concerns. Members should deepen mutual understanding and properly manage differences through communication and dialogue to ensure the steady and long-term development of BRICS cooperation, he said. From its original four members, BRICS has grown into a family of 11 full members and 10 partner countries. Its members account for nearly half the world's population and over one-fourth of global trade. Xi said the grouping's historic expansion and comprehensive, multilevel cooperation framework have ushered in a new stage of high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation. With unilateralism and power politics undermining multilateralism and the international order, BRICS countries should stand firmly on the right side of history, steer the international order toward greater fairness and equity, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity, he said. On innovation-driven development, Xi welcomed BRICS countries' participation in the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, which was launched by China in July and is based in Shanghai, and proposed a BRICS initiative on using AI to advance new industrialization. On peace and stability, Xi noted that the situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid, and said China will work with fellow BRICS members to play a due role in bringing peace and tranquility to the Middle East and the Gulf region. Xi also called for greater mutual learning among civilizations through the BRICS people-to-people exchanges forum, the sharing of governance experience, and deeper cooperation in the areas of culture, tourism and education, including more exchanges among young people. On global governance, he urged support for the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core and called for opposition to all forms of protectionism. BRICS should help shape governance in emerging areas such as cyberspace, outer space and the deep sea, while strengthening the voice of the Global South, he said. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said BRICS has established a distinct identity on the global stage over the past 20 years by respecting different perspectives and moving forward through consensus. AI, cyberspace, outer space, biotechnology and critical technologies are shaping not only future opportunities, but also the rules that will govern the future, Modi said. "We must work to transform the Global South from rule-takers into rule-shapers," he said. The meeting participants highly commended the development achievements made by BRICS over the past two decades, saying that BRICS countries have a responsibility to speak out for the Global South, defend multilateralism and jointly address global challenges in the face of intensifying geopolitical conflicts and rising unilateralism. They said they appreciate China's important contribution to the development and expansion of the BRICS mechanism, and also support China in successfully hosting the 19th BRICS Summit during its presidency next year and working together to push BRICS cooperation to a new level. The summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration of the 18th BRICS Summit. China has been an important participant, builder and promoter of BRICS. Xi has, at different key stages, proposed a series of initiatives for the grouping's development. In 2014, he advocated the BRICS spirit of openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation. In 2017, he proposed the "BRICS Plus" cooperation approach, extending BRICS cooperation beyond its members to the broader Global South. In 2024, he called for a BRICS committed to peace, innovation, green development, justice and closer people-to-people exchanges. Lan Jianxue, director of the Department for Asia-Pacific Studies at the China Institute of International Studies, said these proposals have helped guide and broaden BRICS cooperation, extending it beyond economic ties into a more comprehensive framework. China could draw on its comprehensive industrial system, as well as BRICS' innovation and AI cooperation platforms, to share technologies, conduct joint research and provide training, Lan said. Such efforts could help partner countries develop digital industries and participate more fully in industrial and supply chains. Ayanda Holo, president of TV BRICS Africa, said he looks forward to covering next year's summit in China. Citing China's moves to offer zero-tariff access to African countries with which it has diplomatic relations, Holo said he hopes other BRICS members and partners could also gain greater access to the Chinese market and share in the opportunities created by China's development. During the meeting, leaders from BRICS countries also visited a photo exhibition, planted trees and posed for a group photo.

item.title: Xi: China, India can achieve shared growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-13
Xi: China, India can achieve shared growth Nations urged to provide positive energy for global peace, stability President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that China and India, although having different national conditions, can learn from each other's strengths to achieve shared success and pursue common development. He made the remarks when meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the capital of India. The two leaders had a candid and in-depth exchange of views, reaching an important consensus on China and India being partners. Xi said that amid a complex international situation, China and India — as the two most populous countries and important members of the Global South — bear significant responsibilities. Both countries should keep the future of humanity in mind and the well-being of their peoples at heart, and work together to promote the high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, providing more positive energy for world peace, stability and prosperity, he said. On the development of bilateral relations, Xi urged India to calibrate the direction with an objective and rational strategic understanding, saying that China and India are partners, not rivals, and they represent development opportunities for each other, not threats. Xi underlined the need for both sides to uphold a win-win approach to achieve mutual success. The two countries should expand cooperation in cultural and people-to-people exchanges, as well as increase direct flights, to improve the public opinion foundation of bilateral relations, he said, adding that the two nations should also adopt a balanced approach to address each other's economic and trade concerns. Xi urged eliminating interference with the political wisdom of mutual respect and mutual understanding, saying that the two countries should remain committed to a dual-track approach of advancing bilateral relations and resolving the boundary question, with both reinforcing each other and maintaining peace and tranquility in border areas. He also called for China and India to strengthen coordination within multilateral frameworks in addition to BRICS, such as the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and the Group of 20, and work together to address global challenges and staunchly defend international fairness and justice. During their meeting, Modi assured Xi that India always views its relationship with China from a strategic and long-term perspective. India is willing to be partners with China, rather than rivals, and is ready to view China's development as an opportunity, rather than a challenge, he said. Modi said that India adheres to an independent foreign policy, and its development of relations with China is not influenced by third parties. India's policy and stance on the Taiwan question and issues related to the Xizang autonomous region remain unchanged, and it will not allow any force to engage in anti-China activities in the country, he added. Modi expressed India's readiness to maintain high-level exchanges and strengthen strategic communication with China based on mutual respect and mutual trust, promote mutually beneficial cooperation, and encourage close cultural and people-to-people exchanges to achieve greater development in bilateral relations. He also expressed India's commitment to working with China to maintain peace and tranquility in border areas.

item.title: BRICS' role in economic stability hailed amid intl shocks
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
BRICS' role in economic stability hailed amid intl shocks BRICS can serve as a potential stabilizer for the Global South as emerging economies grapple with overlapping shocks — from climate-driven disruptions to geopolitical conflict and a resurgence of protectionism — that are straining growth and investment, experts say. According to Priyanka Kishore, director and principal economist at the Singapore-based consultancy Asia Decoded, BRICS plays an important role in facilitating dialogue and information-sharing among major emerging economies. For Amitendu Palit, a senior research fellow with the Institute of South Asian Studies at the National University of Singapore, BRICS' biggest appeal is the organization's economic size. The group's 11 members and 10 partner countries account for more than 40 percent of global GDP, giving it the weight to expand trade and investment flows across regions. Greater intra-BRICS commerce would benefit not only the members themselves but also the wider economic zones they anchor, Palit said. Still, he noted that the bloc is far from cohesive enough to function as a rules-based free trade area: its members are geographically dispersed and operate under vastly different political systems, institutions and production standards. On the other hand, those divergences are also what make BRICS a "unique grouping", he said. "If it is able to move forward on its agenda of encouraging more trade in local currencies among members and enhancing food security, then it should be able to provide some solutions to unilateral trade actions elsewhere." Despite its limitations, BRICS, as an intergovernmental organization of developing countries, provides "concrete, nonalignment-friendly mechanisms" to cushion member economies against external vulnerabilities, according to Jaziri Alkaf Abdillah Suffian, chairman of BRICS International Malaysia and a former senator in Malaysia's parliament. Mechanisms developed under BRICS allow full members and partner states to settle bilateral trade using local currencies, he said, and local currency settlements can mitigate exchange rate risk and foreign currency liquidity squeezes during global market crashes. The most recent example of this saw President Xi Jinping and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi welcome the renewal of a bilateral local currency swap agreement and the expansion of the swap scale. The agreement was reached in Cairo when Xi made a state visit to Egypt earlier this month. BRICS has accelerated its push to widen its presence across the Global South. It admitted Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates in early 2024, its biggest expansion since its inception. Indonesia joined as the newest full member in January 2025. India is this year's rotating chair of BRICS, with New Delhi hosting the 18th BRICS Summit. This year's theme is "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability". The summit comes as the Global South faces threats from extreme weather as a result of a likely super El Nino, higher tariffs imposed by the United States, and an escalating crisis in the Middle East that has greatly raised global oil prices. Some economists have said rising demand for artificial intelligence has boosted exports of countries that rank higher in the technology value chain, dampening the impact of higher US tariffs on their economies. This is where BRICS can have a "more meaningful impact", Kishore of Asia Decoded said. Intra-BRICS trade has been rising for the past 20 years, but it still accounts for only about 5 percent of global trade, she said. "By reaffirming its commitment to free trade and strengthening trade engagement between members through instruments such as the proposed BRICS invoice discounting mechanism, it can help member countries diversify away from the US market," she said. prime@chinadailyapac.com

item.title: Expanding voice of Global South
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
Expanding voice of Global South BRICS has proved that it can function as an effective international grouping. Over the years, BRICS members have drawn closer across several sectors, with special emphasis on economic cooperation. The grouping has also expanded its membership, and the enlarged BRICS has become a new reality. Decades of rapid growth have also given some of the grouping's members, such as China, Brazil and India, far more weight in the global economy as producers, exporters and consumers. This growing influence adds to the strength of the grouping. Given its huge potential, the enlarged BRICS can serve as a key forum for widening intra-grouping market access in several ways. Supported by the resources of both the New Development Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, as well as China's Belt and Road Initiative, the grouping can generate a new model of development and modernization for emerging economies and the Global South in general. Such a model would operate independently of the Western-dictated framework that has long shaped global economic governance. The enlarged BRICS could therefore foster and lead a development model focused on South-South cooperation. Through its financial and institutional mechanisms, it can offer alternatives to Western-led financial institutions by promoting local currency financing, reducing dependence on the US dollar and avoiding traditional political and policy conditionalities often attached to international lending. Several BRICS members have already developed successful and independent paths of reform and modernization. China's model of socialism with Chinese characteristics, India's emphasis on high-end knowledge-intensive sectors and Brazil's focus on inclusive growth are important examples of self-designed development strategies. Such development and modernization models offer humanity new choices for achieving reform and genuine development without resorting to what the West calls the "Washington Consensus", promoted by the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. They show that the path to modernization depends on a country's specific political circumstances, social conditions, cultural traditions and historical experience. In other words, there is neither a single development model that should be regarded as the only choice, nor is there a universal modernization model standard for all nations. The Chinese, Indian and Brazilian experiences are therefore very relevant to other Global South nations. Many of the development challenges that China, India and Brazil faced are relevant to other nations, including Egypt. Combating poverty, transitioning to a new growth model, building cost-effective health systems, modernizing agriculture and enhancing industrial productivity are examples of the challenges that all Global South nations face. The enlarged BRICS also provides emerging markets with the opportunity to align on global topics and opens new avenues to promote mutual economic growth. As the grouping continues to develop financial institutions and create new payment mechanisms for cross-border transactions, there could be significant implications for the future of global trade, energy industry, international finance, industrial supply chains, monetary policy and technological innovation. Contrary to misconceptions, the enlarged BRICS is not intended to oppose or antagonize existing international institutions or groups. Rather, its purpose is to offer an alternative perspective within the prevailing global framework, which has long been dominated by Western developed economies. The enlarged BRICS aspires to actively participate in international decision-making and contribute to shaping global policies in ways that reflect its members' local contexts and national priorities. This approach reflects a commitment to more inclusive participation in the international system where each member's voice is heard. As major emerging markets are part of the grouping, BRICS gives the Global South a stronger voice in global economic governance and helps balance the influence of existing Western-controlled institutions. At the same time, there appears to be an intention to prevent the grouping from challenging the US-led global dominance. But some of the US government's actions actually have had the opposite effect. The unilateral policies of the US government and its aggressive "America First" doctrine have brought the grouping and the "middle powers" of the West closer and encouraged many countries in the Global South to pursue alternative frameworks for economic cooperation. While Canada, France and Germany remain anchored in the Western system, the agendas of many "middle powers" align with the multipolar vision of the enlarged BRICS. It's an indication that the future of global trade lies not dominantly across the Atlantic, but with the Global South as well. The US tariff threats have only accelerated this trend. The enlarged BRICS narrative that a more balanced and equitable international order is necessary has been reinforced by Washington's actions. The growing collaboration between the "middle powers" and the enlarged BRICS is therefore driven by necessity and nurtured by shared economic interests. This collaboration will help shape the global order into one that is more balanced, more diverse and less dependent on any single superpower. The author is a former assistant foreign minister of Egypt, former ambassador of Egypt to China and a board member of the Egypt-China Friendship Association. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily.

item.title: US firms display new confidence in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
US firms display new confidence in China Improved financial performance and easing China-US tensions have lifted confidence among United States businesses in China to its highest level since 2021, according to a survey report released on Thursday, signaling a brighter corporate outlook as bilateral trade relations stabilize. The share of respondents who are optimistic about their five-year business outlook in China rose by 17 percentage points to 58 percent, reversing a four-year decline that had pushed the reading to successive record lows, according to the 2026 China Business Report, released by the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai. In contrast, 16 percent of respondents are pessimistic about their five-year business outlook in China, the lowest level since 2021, said the report. It suggested that the improvement in business confidence has coincided with the easing of China-US trade tensions. However, US companies remain cautious about their business in China, keeping a close eye on the market environment and bilateral relations. This year's survey followed several months of positive developments in China-US relations. According to the report, these developments signal a move toward a more predictable and constructive bilateral relationship anchored in strategic stability. "Business confidence has made a critical comeback, supported by stronger financial performance and an improved geopolitical landscape," Jeffrey Lehman, chair of the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai, and Eric Zheng, president of AmCham Shanghai, said in a joint message. According to Lehman and Zheng, optimism about the five-year business outlook in China and the proportion of members reporting profitability last year both reached record levels. Furthermore, a growing percentage of respondents expect their top-line growth to improve this year and outpace their companies' global performance in the near term. Meanwhile, "investment sentiment has recovered, with nearly one-third of respondents planning to increase investment this year", the message added. Profitability among the surveyed companies reached its strongest level since 2019, as 78 percent of respondents were profitable in 2025, up 7 percentage points from the previous year, said the report. Due to differentiated industry dynamics and operating environments, performance continued to vary significantly by sector. Manufacturing, for example, remained the strongest-performing sector, with 85 percent of respondents reporting profits in 2025, a 5-percentage-point increase from the previous year. Services recorded the lowest rate among sectors at 69 percent, but showed a significant year-on-year improvement, rising 14 percentage points. Fifty-five percent of the respondents said that the business environment in China is transparent, up 7 percentage points, the report showed. "China will continue to open its economy wider to the world during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period, while taking further steps to improve the business environment for foreign investors and ensure national treatment for foreign-invested enterprises," said Zhou Haibing, deputy head of the National Development and Reform Commission, during a roundtable meeting of the NDRC and US multinational enterprises in Beijing on Thursday. Stressing the mutually beneficial nature of China-US economic and trade ties, Zhou said that a stable and predictable relationship serves the interests of both countries and the wider world. China is home to 84,000 US-invested companies, with a combined annual revenue of nearly $700 billion, highlighting the strong complementarity and mutual benefits underpinning bilateral economic ties, he said. Given the sheer scale of bilateral economic and trade cooperation, differences and frictions are only natural, Zhou added, noting that solutions can always be found as long as the two sides respect and understand each other and strengthen communication and consultation. US companies' confidence in growth and investment in China comes as foreign companies continue to expand their investment in the country, Xinhua News Agency reported, citing Yan Dong, vice-minister of commerce. The number of new foreign-invested enterprises in China grew 4.4 percent year-on-year during the first seven months of this year, with foreign direct investment in actual use amounting to 438.33 billion yuan ($65.35 billion), according to the Ministry of Commerce. The increase was accompanied by an optimization in the investment structure, with investment in high-tech industries up 32.7 percent year-on-year, accounting for 41.6 percent of the total. "China is a training ground for US companies to maintain their global competitiveness," Lehman and Zheng from AmCham Shanghai said in their joint message. Chinese competitors raise the bar even higher. In the artificial intelligence sector, 43 percent of members view their local competitors as more advanced in AI adoption, the message added. wang_ying@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi attends BRICS summit in New Delhi
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
Xi says BRICS world's most influential platform for emerging markets cooperation NEW DELHI -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said here on Saturday that the BRICS cooperation mechanism has become the world's most influential platform for cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries. When addressing the Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Xi noted that this year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation, saying that over the past two decades, the BRICS cooperation mechanism has continued to grow and expand, and has demonstrated remarkable vitality and dynamism. Xi said it has been 20 years of self-reliance and self-strengthening, adding that BRICS countries have actively explored development paths suited to their own national conditions, setting an example of self-strengthening through unity among emerging markets and developing countries. This has also been 20 years of standing together through thick and thin, Xi noted. BRICS countries, Xi said, have worked together to tackle challenges ranging from the global financial crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic to climate change. The group has remained steadfast in safeguarding the common interests of the Global South, while providing the world with stability and positive momentum, he said. Xi also hailed the past 20 years of BRICS cooperation as fruitful, saying that BRICS countries have undergone a historic expansion, established a comprehensive, multi-tiered framework for cooperation, and ushered in a new stage of high-quality development for greater BRICS cooperation. Xi stressed that the world is undergoing accelerated transformation unseen in a century, the Global South is rapidly growing in strength, and the trend toward a multipolar world is unstoppable. Meanwhile, countercurrents of unilateralism and power politics are surging, multilateralism and the international order are coming under strain, and deficits in peace, development, security and governance continue to widen, he added. He said that BRICS countries should firmly stand on the right side of history, strive to be a pioneer of the times, steer the international order toward greater justice and equity, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity. Xi called on BRICS to pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development. BRICS countries, he said, should firmly seize the initiative, strengthen cooperation in artificial intelligence, encourage open-source development, openness, cooperation and sharing, and push practical cooperation into new areas and to new heights. BRICS countries are welcome to actively participate in the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, he said. China proposed an initiative to promote new industrialization through artificial intelligence among BRICS countries, and is willing to work with all parties to deliver more outcomes in research, development and application, and deepen cooperation in industrial and supply chains, he said. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in upholding peace and stability. BRICS countries should uphold a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, oppose the Cold War mentality and bloc confrontation, reject violations of other countries' sovereignty and interference in their internal affairs, and play a constructive role in resolving hotspot issues, making a distinctive BRICS contribution to finding solutions that address both symptoms and root causes, he said. Noting that the situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid, Xi said this war has inflicted serious losses on the people of all countries in the region, and it is against the common interests of the international community. Xi said he has set out four propositions on safeguarding and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East, which are aimed at de-escalation, ending hostilities and promoting peace. Xi urged relevant parties to keep to the direction of political settlement, and work for a permanent, comprehensive ceasefire. China will work with fellow BRICS members to play a due role in bringing peace and tranquility to the Middle East, he said. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in facilitating mutual learning between civilizations. The countries, he said, should champion the common values of humanity and advocate exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations as well as harmonious coexistence. They should ensure the success of the BRICS forum on people-to-people and cultural exchanges, share experience in state governance, and build positive momentum for the steady development of relations between countries, Xi added. Xi advocated efforts to deepen cooperation in culture, tourism and education, strengthen youth exchanges, and promote more frequent interactions and closer bonds among the peoples. Xi called on BRICS to be a pioneer in reforming and improving global governance. He urged the group to keep pace with the trend toward greater democracy in international relations, promote a more just and equitable global governance system, and uphold the authority of the United Nations. Xi said BRICS should support a multilateral trading system centered on the World Trade Organization, and reject all forms of protectionist measures. The grouping should lead global governance in emerging domains such as cyberspace, outer space and the deep sea, and amplify the voice of Global South countries, he added. Over an extraordinary two-decade journey, solidarity and cooperation have remained the driving force behind the BRICS cause, Xi stressed. Xi called on BRICS members to remain sincere and candid with one another, seek common ground while respecting differences, and respect each other's core concerns. He also urged the group to deepen mutual understanding through communication and dialogue, properly handle differences, and ensure that BRICS cooperation continues to move forward steadily. China, Xi said, will take over as the rotating chair of the BRICS and host the 19th summit next year. The Chinese side stands ready to work with all parties to build consensus, create a better future, and embark on BRICS' third "golden decade," jointly opening up a bright future of prosperity and progress, he added. At the summit, all parties spoke highly of the development achievements made by BRICS over the past 20 years, noting that the BRICS mechanism has broad representation and great potential for development. In the face of escalating geopolitical conflicts and the rise of unilateralism, BRICS countries have a responsibility to speak up for the Global South, uphold multilateralism, support the central role of the United Nations, uphold the sovereign equality of all countries, abide by international law, oppose interference in the internal affairs of other countries, support free trade, and jointly address global challenges, they said. All parties should uphold the BRICS spirit, deepen cooperation across various fields, enhance economic resilience, promote a more just and inclusive international order, and build a secure and prosperous multipolar world, they added. All parties appreciated China's important contribution to the development and expansion of the BRICS mechanism and supported China, as next year's BRICS chair, in successfully hosting the 19th BRICS Summit, so as to jointly bring BRICS cooperation to a new level. The leaders also adopted a joint declaration at the summit.
